title: Public `delegateToImplementation` Allows Unpermissioned State-Changing Delegatecalls
impact: `delegateToImplementation(bytes)` is `public` (not `internal`/`onlyAdmin`). Any external account can invoke **any** state-changing function on the implementation via delegatecall in the delegator's storage context — e.g. force `accrueInterest()`, call `sweepToken()` (which checks `msg.sender == admin`, so protected), or more importantly invoke `_setImplementation` indirectly is blocked by its own `msg.sender == admin` check, but arbitrary calls still allow griefing (forced accruals, gas griefing, manipulating `accrualBlockNumber` timing) and any future implementation function lacking an explicit `msg.sender` guard becomes instantly exposed. This violates the proxy security invariant that only the delegator (or admin) should drive delegatecalls.
